intro.title: What Type of Overthinker Are You?
intro.subtitle: Everyone overthinks. But HOW you overthink says a lot about you.

question.0: It's 2 AM and you can't sleep. What's your brain doing?
question.0a: Replaying that embarrassing thing you said 3 years ago
question.0b: Imagining alternate timelines where you made different choices
question.0c: Rehearsing tomorrow's conversation word by word
question.0d: Listing everything that could possibly go wrong tomorrow
question.1: You're about to meet someone new. What happens in your head?
question.1b: You analyze their every facial expression during the conversation
question.1c: You imagine all 12 possible outcomes of the meeting
question.1d: You replay the conversation for 3 days straight afterwards
question.2: You just sent an important text. Now what?
question.2a: Re-read it 8 times wondering if the period sounds angry
question.2b: Imagine every possible way they might interpret your words
question.2c: Spiral into panic because they read it but haven't replied
question.2d: Draft 5 follow-up messages, send none of them
question.3: Something stressful happens at work. Your reaction?
question.3a: Can't sleep — your mind runs in circles all night
question.3b: Immediately jump to: I'm going to get fired, lose my house, live in a van
question.3c: Build a 47-step contingency plan for every possible outcome
question.3d: Obsess over what you could have done differently
question.4: Your friend seems distant lately. Your thought process?
question.4a: Analyze their last 20 messages for hidden meaning
question.4b: Practice 'Are you mad at me?' in 15 different tones
question.4c: Imagine the 8 reasons they might secretly hate you
question.4d: Lie awake replaying every interaction for clues
question.5: You need to make an important decision. How do you handle it?
question.5a: Research obsessively until you have 47 browser tabs open
question.5b: Focus entirely on what could go wrong with each option
question.5c: Ask everyone you know, then overanalyze all their advice
question.5d: Decide, then immediately second-guess yourself for weeks
question.6: How do you think about the future?
question.6a: Catastrophize about unlikely disasters in vivid detail
question.6b: Create detailed mental simulations of every possible path
question.6c: Lose sleep over things that are literally years away
question.6d: Rehearse hypothetical future conversations that may never happen
question.7: You're overthinking right now. What does THAT look like?
question.7a: Overthinking about how much you overthink (inception!)
question.7b: Analyzing exactly WHY you overthink everything
question.7c: Building theories about your own thought patterns
question.7d: Worrying that overthinking will eventually ruin your life

quiz.midQuiz: Halfway there! Your overthinking profile is taking shape...

spiral.name: 3AM Spiral Thinker
spiral.tagline: Your brain has no off switch, especially at 2 AM.
spiral.description: You're the classic overthinker whose mind kicks into overdrive the moment your head hits the pillow. One thought leads to another, which leads to another, until you're contemplating the meaning of life at 3 AM. Your thoughts don't go in lines — they go in spirals, each loop pulling you deeper. The good news? Your mind never stops working, which means you're incredibly thorough and self-aware.

architect.name: Scenario Architect
architect.tagline: You've already planned for 47 alternate timelines.
architect.description: Your brain is a simulation engine. Before anything happens, you've already imagined every possible outcome, created contingency plans, and mapped out decision trees. You don't just think about what might happen — you build entire mental worlds around possibilities. While others live in one reality, you're simultaneously running scenarios in a dozen parallel universes. This makes you an incredible strategist and problem solver.

rehearser.name: Reply Rehearser
rehearser.tagline: You've practiced this conversation 12 times already.
rehearser.description: Every conversation is a performance you've rehearsed dozens of times. You draft texts in your Notes app before sending them. You practice your responses to questions nobody has asked yet. You know exactly what you'd say if someone brought up that topic — because you've prepared a 3-minute speech about it in the shower. Your conversations are never spontaneous, but they're always polished.

analyst.name: Micro-Expression Analyst
analyst.tagline: Did they blink twice? That means something.
analyst.description: You notice everything. The slight pause before someone answers, the barely perceptible change in their tone, the way they looked at their phone during your story. Your brain is a pattern-recognition machine tuned to pick up social signals that most people miss. You read between every line and behind every smile. While this can be exhausting, it also makes you incredibly empathetic and emotionally intelligent.

catastrophizer.name: Future Catastrophizer
catastrophizer.tagline: My hobby? Imagining worst-case scenarios in 4K.
catastrophizer.description: A small problem doesn't exist in your world — every issue immediately escalates to its most dramatic conclusion. Got a headache? Probably a brain tumor. Boss wants to talk? You're getting fired. Friend didn't text back? They hate you forever. Your brain is a disaster movie director, always ready to produce the next blockbuster catastrophe. But here's the thing — you're also the most prepared person in any room because you've already survived every worst-case scenario in your head.

replayer.name: Selective Memory Replayer
replayer.description: Your brain is a time machine that exclusively travels to your most embarrassing moments. That awkward thing you said at a party in 2015? Crystal clear. The time you waved back at someone who wasn't waving at you? Replayed nightly. You have a photographic memory, but only for moments you'd rather forget. While you can't remember where you put your keys, you can recall every cringeworthy detail of that conversation from 7 years ago.
